extracted.intended_audience: journalists and press officers (including freelance journalists registered with EurekAlert! and science bloggers of good standing)
extracted.subtask_description: Institutional guidelines for how journalists and press officers must handle embargoed PLOS press materials, including who may access them, timing rules, sharing restrictions, attribution, and enforcement. Focused on ensuring fair, accurate media coverage of peer-reviewed PLOS articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the embargo policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Our embargo policy provides fair and equal opportunity for journalists to research stories and to speak with experts, for researchers to provide comments and for press officers to coordinate coverage with scientists at their institutions. Our embargoes enable authors to achieve accurate, high-quality media coverage which disseminates their peer-reviewed research to non-expert readers. They ensure that peer-reviewed published articles are accessible to everyone when first reported in the media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embargoes exist to give time for accurate reporting, expert comment, and coordination with scientists; they also ensure articles are publicly accessible when media coverage appears.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo timing (PLOS default)
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS articles are embargoed until 11:00 a.m. Pacific Standard Time, 2:00 p.m. Eastern Standard Time on the date of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precise embargo dates and times will be clearly marked on all embargoed materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to access embargoed materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists and freelancers writing for publications that are registered with EurekAlert! are eligible to receive embargoed materials from PLOS. Science bloggers of good standing may also be eligible. All recipients must agree to follow the terms of the embargo policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals who break the embargo policy will be removed from PLOS’ press list for a period to be determined by PLOS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access and attribution requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All content published by PLOS is open access and distributed under a Creative Commons Attribution (CC BY) license. You should credit the appropriate PLOS journal in your coverage and provide a link to the freely available article in any online coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always credit the PLOS journal and include a link to the article when reporting; the CC BY license governs reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on publishing before the embargo
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories or reports on accepted PLOS articles may not be published, broadcast, posted online or on social media or placed in the public domain before the embargo date and time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embargoed materials are explicitly not for public dissemination until the marked embargo date and time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargoed materials are for background research only
rubrics_metrics.description: Embargoed materials are for background research only. Journalists may share embargoed materials only with experts in the field to seek comment, but such materials must be clearly identified as embargoed and must include the embargo date and time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When sharing for comment, label materials as embargoed and include the embargo date/time so recipients know they must not publish before that time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalists’ responsibility to ensure third parties honor embargo
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists are responsible for taking all necessary steps to ensure that third parties honor the embargo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before sharing embargoed materials or expert contacts, confirm recipients understand and will respect the embargo; failure to do so can lead to removal from press lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press officers: restrictions on distribution and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Press officers may not distribute embargoed materials in the public domain before the embargo date. However, embargoed materials may be distributed to the media by press officers up to seven days before the embargo date. Press releases must be clearly identified as embargoed and must include the embargo date and time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press officers may circulate embargoed press releases to media up to seven days prior, but must label them clearly and include embargo metadata; they must also take steps to ensure third parties honor the embargo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance notice provided by PLOS
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS will provide advance notice of press-released articles to members of its press list up to seven days ahead of publication. Distribution and use of all advance materials are subject to the PLOS embargo policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving advance materials from PLOS does not imply permission to publish before the embargo; use and distribution remain governed by the policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: No exclusives policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Please note that PLOS does not grant exclusives to journalists or news outlets, and neither may authors or press officers unilaterally grant exclusives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not promise or accept exclusive coverage based on PLOS embargoed materials; exclusivity is not permitted by PLOS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement: consequences for breaching the embargo
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals who break the embargo policy will be removed from PLOS’ press list for a period to be determined by PLOS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breach consequences are removal from press lists; the duration is at PLOS' discretion.
